I’ve seen discussions about the safety netting left up during SKZ’s concert in Fukuoka. As a J-STAY, I wanted to share a bit of context!

PayPay Dome is owned by the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks (Japan's "NY Yankees"), who installed a huge 21-meter (69 ft) safety net this year. Venue rules require flawless restoration after events—even a single lost bolt on the field could cause a career-ending injury for a player. Stage teardown normally takes two full days.

During the 2023 tour, SKZ played on Wed/Thu to allow teardown time before a Saturday game. This time, the show was Saturday, and a critical playoff game was Sunday afternoon.

The concert ended at 10:30 PM, and baseball doors opened at 4:00 PM the next day. The crew had to finish a 2-day job in just 17 hours, working straight through the night. Leaving the net up was a painful compromise to save crucial time.
